fields.meta_title: Home Care Intake Form Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a home care intake form that starts with the family's first call and ends in a care schedule your scheduler can staff.
fields.h1: Build a Home Care Intake Form From First Call to First Shift
fields.hero_description: Describe your agency and how your care managers assess a new client. Emergent builds the home care intake form and the client record behind it, down to the schedule request.
fields.explore_cta: Build My Home Care Intake Form
fields.features_heading: What a Home Care Client Record Holds
fields.features_subheading: The answers a care manager needs before the first visit, and the ones a scheduler needs before the first shift.
fields.feature_1:
Family contacts in calling order

List the client and every relative who should hear from the agency, numbered in the order to call. Mark who can approve a change to care and who only wants updates after visits.
fields.feature_2:
Daily activities scored one by one

Score each self-care task, such as bathing or transfers, on one scale from independent to full help. Household tasks like meals and laundry sit in a second group right below them.
fields.feature_3:
Home safety walk-through by room

Give the assessor a checklist for each room of the house. Every hazard marked yes needs a photo and a short note, and it becomes a line in the care plan the family signs.
fields.feature_4:
A schedule request, not a paragraph

Ask for the days and hours of each visit as separate fields. Add caregiver preferences like language or pets at home, then compare them with each caregiver on your staff list.
fields.feature_5:
Payer type on the first screen

Ask whether care is private pay, long-term care insurance or a VA benefit. Each answer then loads the follow-up questions billing needs for that payer, like a policy number.
fields.feature_6:
Source code in your own repo

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can connect the intake to your agency's scheduling system and keep changing it there for years after launch.

fields.usecase_heading: Intake at Four Home Care Agencies
fields.tab_content_1:
Called from Denver about a father in Tucson

Most first calls at Larkspur Home Care come from adult children, and the inquiry form starts with whoever is filling it in. Elena Ruiz lists herself as first call and her brother Marco as second, then describes her father's week. Intake coordinator Rosa Delgado gets the request with two assessment times to offer.
fields.tab_content_2:
Four hours a day, set by three needs-help answers

Care managers at Juniper Home Care score each daily activity on a tablet during the home visit. Walter Hayes needs help with bathing, dressing and getting out of a chair. Three needs-help answers set his starting plan at four hours a day, which the care manager can adjust before the family signs.
fields.tab_content_3:
By the tub, no grab bar; in the hall, a loose rug

Fernhill Senior Care's assessors walk each house room by room with a checklist on their phone. At June Park's home, Dana Moss flags two hazards: a loose rug in the hallway and a tub with no grab bar. Both go into June's care plan with a photo each, and her son Daniel gets the list by email that evening.
fields.tab_content_4:
Who speaks Spanish, works mornings and likes cats

Cobalt Bay Home Care asks new clients for visit times and caregiver preferences as separate fields. Carmen Vidal wants Tuesday and Thursday mornings with a Spanish-speaking caregiver who is fine with her cat. Her record shows the scheduler the two caregivers, out of nine on staff, who match every request.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Home Care Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Your intake already happens on the phone and in the client's living room. The form records both conversations in the order your agency has them.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Split intake into call and visit
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Start with the person who called
fields.howto_step_1_des: Map intake the way your agency already runs it: a first call that decides whether a visit is worth booking, then an in-home assessment that sets the plan. List what your coordinator and your care managers ask today.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask who is filling in the form and how they are related to the client before any question about care. Collect each family contact with a phone number, the order to call them and whether they can approve changes.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give every activity the same three answers: independent, needs help, full help. Keep self-care such as bathing and toileting apart from chores around the house, because the two groups often lead to different services.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give the assessor a section per room with yes or no questions about rugs, grab bars, stair rails and lighting at the top of the stairs. Require a photo whenever the assessor marks a hazard yes. The family then sees exactly what was found.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your questions and your rules, such as which scores set the starting hours. Emergent builds the form and the client table from that prompt. Ask for changes later in plain English, like a new payer type or an extra room.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the agreed schedule and caregiver preferences to the scheduling software your office uses, and the payer details to billing. Emergent connects to any tool with an API, and every record stays in a database your agency owns.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run a test client through it
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in an inquiry as a relative would, then complete an assessment on a tablet as your care manager would in the home. Check the family email, the care plan lines and the schedule request before a real client sees any of it.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is a Jotform app template, fill-and-sign PDFs on DocHub and signNow, Etsy document packets, an agency software newsletter and a 2016 blog post listing height, weight and diagnosis. None of them follows how a non-medical home care agency takes on a client: a family member calls first, a care manager visits the home, and the answers become a schedule and a caregiver match. This page builds that intake as one client record, from the first family inquiry through the ADL assessment and home safety walk-through to the hours and caregiver preferences the scheduler works from.
tab_stories: A daughter in Denver fills in the inquiry form for her father in Tucson, lists herself and her brother as the people to call, and Larkspur Home Care's intake coordinator gets the request with two assessment times to offer.

At the in-home assessment, a Juniper Home Care care manager marks each daily activity on a tablet as independent, needs help or full help, and three activities marked needs help set the starting plan at four hours a day.
A Fernhill Senior Care assessor walks the house room by room, and the two hazards she flags, a loose hallway rug and a tub with no grab bar, go into the care plan and to the family by email.
A client of Cobalt Bay Home Care asks for Tuesday and Thursday mornings with a Spanish-speaking caregiver who is fine with cats, and the scheduler sees the two caregivers who match all three.
